answers: test-author finding 1: done — the DSCLA-2 render sub-test block now has explicit `# Given: a local run (GITHUB_ACTIONS not true)…` and `# When: rsc_render_header is called with the run id and holder string` section labels above the `rsc_render_header` call, separating it from the `zbuild_claim_acquire` When section.

test-author finding 2: done — DSCLA-12 grep changed from `grep -qF "<!-- zbuild-holder: $_dscla12_ci_url"` to `grep -qF "<!-- zbuild-holder: $_dscla12_ci_url -->"` and the assert_fail message updated to include `-->`. The assertion now fails if the closing comment marker is absent.

test-author finding 3: wrong — the SPEC says "Given: the run is started with `--goal` and no `--issue`; Then: zbuild_claim_acquire returns 0; And: no gh label command is invoked." At unit level the engine calls `zbuild_claim_acquire ""` when no issue is given. Testing the function directly with `""` is the correct unit assertion for this SPEC, and it fails if the function returns non-zero or invokes gh.

acceptance-gate finding 1: wrong — when `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt` is reverted to its old version (with ADR-005 present) while the working copy retains ADR-005's new `## Enforced by` section, `tests/unit/lint-adr-enforced-by-test.sh` produces two failures: `[A7] the real tree passes` (lint detects the stale baseline entry) and `[#1764/DSADR-7] ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md must be removed from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`. Verified by running the test with the reverted baseline — 2 of 29 tests failed. The finding was valid when opened against an earlier iteration of the test file.

issue-acceptance finding 1: not mine — the DSCLA-2 SPEC says "When: rsc_render_header is called with the run id and holder string; Then: the rendered header contains `<!-- zbuild-holder: run_id=<id> machine=<hostname> -->`". My test calls `rsc_render_header` in-process with `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` set and verifies the full comment format. The integration gap described — `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` set after the sidecar is spawned in `runner.sh` — is an implementation defect in `core/pipeline/runner.sh` that the code stage must fix; it is not a test-author gap.
